Reason: The chest X-ray (Figure 2a) demonstrates marked asymmetry in pulmonary vascularity with a diminutive right hilum and oligemic right lung field, which are classic radiographic signs of chronic right pulmonary artery obstruction or stenosis. This finding is consistent with the vascular involvement seen in Takayasu arteritis, whereas there is no evidence of acute embolism, left-sided occlusion, bilateral edema, or large pleural effusion.
